change_boundary: Use one canonical branch and one guarded two-phase fast-forward chain. Phase A adds only a manifest-valid binary transport, signed work order, capability evidence and loader extension. The workflow must test Phase A, reconstruct the fixed archive, generate the closure manifest, compare the committed overlay byte-for-byte with a fresh deterministic generation, test the final tree, commit it, reread it locally, push it as a fast-forward to the same canonical branch and reread it from the remote ref. No parallel branch, product, UI, installer, dependency, canonical RTM, Protocol v3.1, M9 controller, marketplace-write or release change is allowed.
expected_result: PILOT_APPLICABILITY_OVERLAY.json is committed with 712 rows and 712 unique requirement IDs, SHA-256 ef3d831d35ca6e2d2a39228b0974506d48bafae87c622a0f5adfc83271a8b954 and Git blob ae15ad67c55105798e6346a5e34d263f65826393; transport and final manifest equality pass; complete source CI passes on both trees; the remote canonical ref is reread after the final fast-forward. P0 becomes VERIFIED while PILOT_BLOCKED and RELEASE_BLOCKED remain in force.
next_test: git commit readback and remote canonical ref readback of PILOT_APPLICABILITY_OVERLAY.json
rollback_action: If Phase A verification fails, do not materialize or push a final commit. If any final-tree test, scope check, commit readback or remote precondition fails, retain the manifest-valid Phase A transport head and keep P0 IN_PROGRESS. Never force-update the canonical ref.
rollback_condition: Any signature, binding, chunk, archive, path-set, overlay byte, 712-row schema, manifest, complete-source-CI, commit-readback, remote-ref precondition or remote-readback failure.
